Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund
Sponsor: Albritton
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 361 as introduced could increase the obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles, by an undetermined amount, by authorizing the Board of Pardons and Paroles to: (1) increase the amount of funds that may be awarded for outstanding employee performance from $250 per year to $500 per year; and (2) expend funds appropriated to recruit and train law enforcement officers and support staff, educating the public, and promoting the agency's mission. The amount of the increased obligations would depend upon the amount set by the Board to be awarded for outstanding employee performance and the costs associated with the recruitment and training of law enforcement officers and support staff.
Greg Albritton, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation General Fund

Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund
Sponsor: Albritton

Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 361 as introduced could increase the obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles, by an undetermined amount, by authorizing the Board of Pardons and Paroles to: (1) increase the amount of funds that may be awarded for outstanding employee performance from $250 per year to $500 per year; and (2) expend funds appropriated to recruit and train law enforcement officers and support staff, educating the public, and promoting the agency's mission. The amount of the increased obligations would depend upon the amount set by the Board to be awarded for outstanding employee performance and the costs associated with the recruitment and training of law enforcement officers and support staff.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation General Fund, could decrease the obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles, by an undetermined amount, by removing the $250 award for outstanding employee performance.
Greg Albritton, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation General Fund

Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Albritton
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/13/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 361 as passed the Senate authorizes the Board of Pardons and Paroles to expend funds appropriated for recruitment materials and training law enforcement officers and support staff, educating the public, and promoting the agencys mission. In addition, this bill (1) removes the current limitation that a parole or probation officer be assigned no more than 20 active high-risk cases at any time; and (2) disallows the Board to provide incentive awards up to $250 per year for outstanding employee performance.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Brown (C)
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/15/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 131 as passed the House of Representatives proposes a Constitutional Amendment which, if ratified, would continue to entitle every person charged with a crime pretrial bail unless the individual is charged with an offense enumerated by the Legislature.
This bill will increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from the State General Fund, by an estimated $100,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary
